category_title: Students with severe intellectual disability (SID) using pre-symbolic or limited symbolic communication and idiosyncratic repair strategies
minimal_context: The student is participating in a daily routine classroom activity and attempting to communicate a want during snack time.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our morning snack routine. Here is your empty cup.

STUDENT: (Makes eye contact, uses facial expressions, and makes sounds while approaching the tutor to sign her wants for the juice pitcher.)

TUTOR: Just sit down in your chair.

STUDENT: (Changes posture, shouts, and approaches the pitcher again, using idiosyncratic behaviors to communicate her intent.)

TUTOR: Look at the cup on your table.

STUDENT: (Withdraws completely from the table, drops eye contact, and terminates all communication attempts, resulting in complete communication arrest.)

options.A: Request clarification from the student during the snack routine, asking for explanations and elaborations about what she wants.
options.B: Teach specific self-regulation strategies during the snack routine, such as going to a quiet place, using a blanket, or counting to ten.
options.C: Explain that the snack routine is completed step by step, and when finished, she will have free time to play and relax.
options.D: Follow through to ensure she complies with the direction to look at the cup if she does not do it independently.
